title: Chat: custom/rich in-bubble content via render prop
description: Beyond markdown, real chat apps put arbitrary React into a bubble: correction cards, inline audio/TTS buttons, citations, tool-call chips. The practice app needs this (e.g. a '✏️ «x» → «y»' correction card and a speak button per assistant turn). Add an escape hatch so consumers control bubble body rendering without forking Chat.
design: Add optional 'renderMessage?: (msg: ChatMessage) => ReactNode' to ChatProps; when provided, Chat calls it for the bubble body instead of the default text/markdown path, but still owns layout, alignment, key, timestamp, auto-scroll, and a11y (aria-live). Alternatively allow ChatMessage.content?: ReactNode. Keep 'text: string' required for accessibility/copy fallback even when custom content is supplied. This subsumes markdown for power users but markdown (sibling bead) stays as the ergonomic default.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Passing renderMessage renders custom nodes inside correctly-aligned user/other bubbles. 2) Default rendering unchanged when renderMessage is omitted. 3) Timestamp, auto-scroll, and aria-live still work with custom content. 4) TypeScript types exported. 5) Test + Storybook story showing a custom bubble (e.g. a card + button).
close_reason: Closed

title: Chat: streaming / incremental assistant updates + busy state
description: LLM replies stream token-by-token. Consumers update a message's text repeatedly as chunks arrive. Chat auto-scrolls on the messages array reference changing (useEffect deps: [messages]), which works if consumers pass a new array each tick, but there's no first-class 'assistant is responding' affordance (typing indicator / disabled send / loader) and no documented streaming contract.
design: Add an optional 'busy?: boolean' (or 'status?: 'idle'|'streaming'') prop that (a) shows a typing/loader affordance in the list and (b) optionally disables/annotates the send button. Document the streaming contract: mutate the last message's text and pass a new array reference to trigger scroll. Ensure auto-scroll only forces to bottom when the user is already near the bottom (don't yank the viewport if they've scrolled up to read history). Reuse the existing Loader/Skeleton component for the indicator.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Setting busy shows a typing indicator and reflects on the composer. 2) Rapidly updating the last message's text scrolls smoothly without flicker. 3) If the user scrolls up, incoming updates do NOT force-scroll them to the bottom. 4) aria-live announces new/updated assistant content politely, not on every token. 5) Test + Storybook story simulating a streamed reply.
close_reason: Closed

title: Chat: opt-in markdown rendering in message bubbles
description:
Chat currently renders message text as a plain text node (Chat.tsx:
{msg.text}
). LLM output is markdown — bold, lists, code spans/blocks, links, paragraphs — and renders as raw asterisks/backticks today. Add opt-in markdown rendering per message or per Chat instance.
design: Add a 'format' discriminator to ChatMessage (e.g. format?: 'text' | 'markdown', default 'text') OR a Chat-level prop 'renderMarkdown?: boolean'. Prefer per-message so a single conversation can mix plain and rich. Ship a small, dependency-free markdown renderer (Azimuth advertises 'zero external dependencies' — do NOT pull in marked/react-markdown into the core bundle; either implement a minimal safe subset or expose a 'renderText' hook so consumers inject their own). MUST sanitize: never dangerouslySetInnerHTML raw model output without escaping/sanitizing — treat all message text as untrusted. Respect prefers-reduced-motion and existing bubble styles.
acceptance_criteria: 1) A message with format:'markdown' containing **bold**, a list, a code block, and a link renders as HTML, not literal syntax. 2) A message with format:'text' (or unset) renders exactly as today (no behavior change; snapshot stable). 3) No XSS: a message containing /

title: Chat: production-grade conversation surface (markdown, rich content, streaming, multiline)
description:
Umbrella for Chat enhancements needed to make it usable as the primary surface of a real LLM/tutor app instead of a demo widget. Children cover: markdown rendering, custom bubble content (render prop), multiline composer, streaming/incremental updates + busy state, and a configurable header/empty-state. Each is independently shippable and backward compatible (opt-in props; existing plain-text behavior stays the default).

## Context
Driven by integrating azimuth-ui into the Learning Lab practice app (a language-tutor chat on top of `opencode serve`). The current Chat component renders plain-text bubbles only: {msg.text} as a text node, a single-line <input>, a hardcoded 'Chat' header, and user/other senders. Real LLM chat UIs need markdown, streaming, rich in-bubble content, and multiline composition. This epic tracks bringing Chat up to that bar so consuming apps don't have to fork it.

title: Set up accessibility tooling: Storybook a11y addon, eslint-plugin-jsx-a11y, axe-core
description:
Per dev friend's recommendation — AI alone is not sufficient for accessibility. Need layered tooling:

1. **@storybook/addon-a11y** — Runs axe-core against every .stories.tsx in the test runner. Catches violations per component variant as part of CI.

2. **eslint-plugin-jsx-a11y** — Catches static JSX issues: missing alt text, invalid ARIA, label associations, click handlers without keyboard handlers. Estimated to catch 30-40% of real a11y issues.

3. **@axe-core/react** — Logs a11y violations to the dev console at runtime during development. Catches dynamic issues that linters miss.

Setup steps:
1. npm install --save-dev @storybook/addon-a11y eslint-plugin-jsx-a11y @axe-core/react
2. Add @storybook/addon-a11y to .storybook/main.ts addons array
3. Add axe-core initialization to src/main.tsx or demo entry (for dev-only logging)
4. Add eslint-plugin-jsx-a11y to eslint.config.js
5. Run the Storybook test runner against all stories to establish baseline
6. Document the tooling layers and their limitations in CONTRIBUTING.md

title: Add CI workflow for push/PR and harden prepublishOnly gates
description:
CI must run on EVERY push (all branches) and every PR — not just deploys. Whatever lands on main must have passed lint + tests.

Changes:

1. Create .github/workflows/ci.yml:
   on: [push, pull_request]
   steps: npm ci → npm run lint → npm run typecheck → npm run test → npm run build
   This runs on every push to any branch, giving immediate feedback when working in branches.

2. Add lint to .github/workflows/publish.yml (currently has typecheck + test + build but no lint).

3. Update prepublishOnly in package.json to chain all gates:
   "prepublishOnly": "npm run lint && npm run typecheck && npm run test && npm run build"

4. (Optional) Set up branch protection on GitHub to require CI to pass before merge, to force the habit of branching + PRs.

CI on push means: even if you push directly to main, lint + tests run and failures are visible. CI on all branches means you get the same safety when experimenting with branches — lowering the friction to start using them.
notes: User workflow: pushes directly to main (no branches/PRs). CI must run on push to main, not require PRs. For npm: manual deploy script creates chore/version-bump branch, bumps version, auto-merges to main.

title: Theming: consumer stylesheet cannot override inline-set --azimuth-* tokens (radius/space/shadow/font); re-verify color-var repro on 0.9.3
description:
PARTIALLY ADDRESSED since 0.2.0: ThemeProvider (src/theme/ThemeProvider.tsx) now injects a <style data-azimuth-light/dark> block into <head> defining color vars under [data-theme] / :root (the surface/border/text vars the consumer had to set manually are now shipped — see closed azimuth-ui-qlk). So the original 'missing color vars' half is likely fixed. RESIDUAL, still true in 0.9.3: radius, space, shadow, font, and ease tokens are applied via setCSSVar -> document.documentElement.style.setProperty (ThemeProvider.tsx ~L78-218). Inline styles on :root beat any consumer stylesheet rule by specificity, so a consumer CANNOT override those token groups from their own CSS — only via JS or the ThemeProvider config. Also the injected color <style> is appended to <head>; whether a consumer's own stylesheet can override it depends on load order (equal :root specificity → source order), which is fragile.

## Context
Re-homed from a stale side tracker (was AZ-m8v, reported against azimuth-ui ^0.2.0 by consuming app job_search_agent, Next.js 15 App Router). title: Light theme accent copper (#e8734a) on-accent (white) fails WCAG AA at 3.01:1
description:
Discovered while investigating azimuth_ui-8hu. The light-theme accent color --azimuth-accent: #e8734a (Copper, oklch ~62% 0.16 35deg) used with --azimuth-color-on-accent (white, oklch 99% 0 0) computes to only 3.01:1 contrast — fails WCAG 2.2 AA (needs 4.5:1). This is the genuine accent contrast failure in the design system (the primary button was misdiagnosed in 8hu — the oklch primary oklch(50% 0.13 195deg) actually passes at 5.29:1; only its broken hex fallback failed).

CONFIRMED via culori (authoritative, sRGB gamut-mapped):
- accent #e8734a vs white: 3.01:1 FAIL
- accent-hover oklch(60% 0.18 35deg) -> #d64c29 vs white: 4.26:1 FAIL (narrowly)

SCOPE: Button has no 'accent' variant, so this does not affect Button contrast directly. It affects any component that fills a background with --azimuth-color-accent and overlays --azimuth-color-on-accent (white) text/icons — e.g. filled Badge accent variant, NotificationBadge, Hero CTA accents. Needs an audit of accent-as-filled-bg usages.

FIX OPTIONS (deliberately deferred from 8hu per maintainer decision):
1. Darken Copper from #e8734a (~oklch 62% 0.16 35) to a darker copper that hits >=4.5:1 with white (e.g. oklch ~52-54% 0.16 35 -> verify). Changes the committed Copper accent app-wide (DESIGN.md says Copper is 'reserved, used sparingly').
2. Keep Copper #e8734a for non-text accent uses (borders, icons, small marks) and only use a darker variant when accent is a filled background with text. Introduce --azimuth-color-accent-strong or reuse on-accent=dark text for filled accent surfaces.
3. Use dark text on filled accent surfaces (--azimuth-color-on-accent -> dark) instead of white. Preserves Copper vibrancy but changes the 'on Copper = white' semantic.

The new token-contrast test (src/styles/__tests__/tokens.contrast.test.ts) currently covers filled-BUTTON variants only (primary/secondary/danger) since Button has no accent variant. If accent is darkened or a filled-accent usage is added to Button, extend the test's PAIRS to include accent/on-accent.
close_reason: Added --azimuth-color-accent-strong token in all four blocks: light oklch oklch(56% 0.16 35deg) -> #c0482a (5.00:1 vs white), dark = var(--azimuth-color-accent) (already 7.01:1), and matching hex values in both fallback blocks. Swapped filled-accent backgrounds to accent-strong in NotificationBadge (.accent), Chip (.accent.selected), ProductCard (.badge), Timeline (.dot) — the four components that overlay on-accent (white) text on an accent-filled background. ProgressBar (accent fill with no text overlay) and all non-text accent usages (borders, accent-text on transparent, accent-subtle bgs) keep the base Copper #e8734a per DESIGN.md's 'Copper Rule' (reserved, used sparingly). Extended the token-contrast test with the accent-filled/on-accent pair across all four theme/path blocks (29 assertions total, all pass). Copper brand color unchanged for non-text uses; only filled-accent-with-text surfaces render slightly darker for AA compliance. All 1505 tests pass, typecheck+lint clean. Files: src/styles/tokens.css, src/styles/__tests__/tokens.contrast.test.ts, NotificationBadge.module.css, Chip.module.css, ProductCard.module.css, Timeline.module.css.

title: Default light theme: primary button text (on-primary on primary) is 3.28:1 — fails WCAG AA for normal text
description: In the bundled light theme, --azimuth-color-primary is #2e9e8e and --azimuth-color-on-primary is #fff. White on #2e9e8e computes to 3.28:1, which fails WCAG 2.2 AA for normal-size text (needs 4.5:1) and only passes the 3:1 large-text threshold. So default primary Buttons with normal-size labels fail AA out of the box. (Hover #258a7c is 4.2:1 — still under 4.5.) FIX options: darken --azimuth-color-primary in the light theme so white text reaches >=4.5:1 (e.g. around #1f7d70 or darker — verify), or lighten/adjust so a dark on-primary is used, whichever keeps the intended teal. Check every bundled theme's primary/secondary/danger/accent vs their on-* tokens for the same 4.5:1 threshold.
acceptance_criteria: Every filled-variant button in every bundled theme meets >=4.5:1 text contrast for normal text at rest and hover; add an automated token-contrast test.
close_reason: Fixed the actual root cause: the oklch primary oklch(50% 0.13 195deg) already passes AA at 5.29:1 (verified via culori); the reported 3.28:1 came from the broken hex fallback #2e9e8e in the @supports not (color: oklch) block, which is a poor approximation of the oklch color. Replaced fallback #2e9e8e->#00787a (5.29:1) and #258a7c->#006b6d (6.32:1) in tokens.css so non-oklch browsers also pass AA. Added automated token-contrast test (src/styles/__tests__/tokens.contrast.test.ts) using culori that asserts primary/secondary/danger variants (rest+hover) >=4.5:1 in light+dark, both oklch and fallback paths (25 assertions, all pass). Discovered accent copper #e8734a fails AA at 3.01:1 — filed as azimuth_ui-yfc (discovered-from this issue) and deferred per maintainer decision. Files: src/styles/tokens.css, src/styles/__tests__/tokens.contrast.test.ts, package.json (+culori devDep), package-lock.json.

title: Button primary:hover swaps background without re-asserting text color — contrast can break per theme
description: In Button.module.css, '.Button_primary' sets 'background: var(--azimuth-color-primary); color: var(--azimuth-color-on-primary);' but '.Button_primary:hover:not(:disabled)' only sets 'background: var(--azimuth-color-primary-hover);' — it does not re-declare color or use an on-primary-hover token. on-primary is chosen for contrast against primary; if a theme's --azimuth-color-primary-hover has a different lightness than --azimuth-color-primary, the fixed on-primary text can lose contrast on hover. This is a latent per-theme fragility (same pattern in .SplitButton_primary:hover). FIX: either keep hover lightness close to base and document the invariant, or introduce --azimuth-color-on-primary-hover and set color on the hover rule so contrast is guaranteed regardless of the hover background. Do the same for secondary/danger/accent hover states.
acceptance_criteria: Primary (and other filled) button text meets >=4.5:1 against the hover background in every bundled theme; add a contrast test or Storybook a11y check for button hover states.
close_reason: Added --azimuth-color-on-primary-hover and --azimuth-color-on-accent-hover tokens across all four token blocks (light oklch, dark oklch, light fallback hex, dark fallback hex) in tokens.css. Wired color: var(--azimuth-color-on-primary-hover) onto .primary:hover in both Button.module.css and SplitButton.module.css so hover text color is now guaranteed against the hover background regardless of theme. Secondary uses fixed text on light surface/surface-hover (passes; no token needed); danger already re-asserts color on hover. The new token-contrast test (src/styles/__tests__/tokens.contrast.test.ts) asserts primary:hover passes >=4.5:1 in every theme/path, guarding the invariant. All 1501 tests pass; lint+typecheck clean.

3. --azimuth-fs-h5 (1.25rem) == --azimuth-fs-xl (1.25rem) and --azimuth-fs-h4 (1.5rem) == --azimuth-fs-2xl (1.5rem) — redundant naming.

title: Security: Pin CI actions to full commit SHAs
description:
CI/CD audit found mutable action tags in .github/workflows/ci.yml:

- oxsecurity/megalinter@v7 (mutable tag, NOT pinned to SHA)
- actions/checkout@v4 and actions/setup-node@v4 are also major-version tags

Best practice: Pin all GitHub Actions to immutable commit SHAs (e.g., actions/checkout@ee0669bd...) with a comment noting the version. This prevents supply-chain attacks where a tag is moved to point at malicious code.

Migrate to Dependabot for automatic SHA updates: add .github/dependabot.yml.

title: Component CSS font-family declarations lack CSS fallback values, causing FOUT with serif fonts on first paint
description: Component CSS files use `font-family: var(--azimuth-font-display)` and `font-family: var(--azimuth-font-body)` without CSS fallback values. The `--azimuth-font-*` CSS variables are set by ThemeProvider in a `useEffect` (JS runtime), so before React hydrates the variables are undefined. Most browsers default to serif when font-family is invalid/unresolved, causing a FOUT (Flash of Unstyled Text) for ~50-200ms before hydration.
notes:
Affected files need fallback added:
- src/components/navigation/Navbar/Navbar.module.css lines 19, 164
- src/components/display/Text/Text.module.css lines 8, 15
- All component CSS using var(--azimuth-font-body) (~30 files)

Fix: Add CSS fallback to every font-family declaration:
`font-family: var(--azimuth-font-body, system-ui, sans-serif)`
`font-family: var(--azimuth-font-display, system-ui, sans-serif)`
`font-family: var(--azimuth-font-mono, ui-monospace, 'Cascadia Code', 'Fira Code', monospace)`

Longer-term: Inject font variables synchronously via <script> tag (like ThemeScript does for color-scheme) to eliminate FOUT entirely.

title: Card component has overflow: hidden — clips expanded content
description:
The Card component has 'overflow: hidden' in its CSS, which clips child content that extends beyond the card boundary. This is problematic for expandable/collapsible content like compliance audit findings groups, accordions, or any card that dynamically grows.

title: InfoButton popover should overlay, not shift layout

Observed in project-bootstrapper: when InfoButton is placed next to step descriptions, the popover content pushes sibling elements around when visible.

Fix: render the popover content via a portal (createPortal to document.body) or use position: fixed with proper coordinates relative to the trigger button. Use a small arrow/pointer to indicate which InfoButton triggered it.

title: Dark mode contrast — Input, ProgressBar, and general surface visibility
description:
When ThemeProvider mode is set to 'system' and the OS is in dark mode, several components have poor contrast:

1. **Input** — text input has a border/background that blends into the dark surface, making the input field nearly invisible
2. **ProgressBar** — the track/background fills are dark-on-dark in dark mode
3. **Placeholder text** — placeholder color is too similar to the input text color in dark mode

The ThemeProvider correctly sets data-theme='dark' on <html> and injects dark CSS variables, but the default dark values may not provide sufficient contrast ratios for these components.

Steps to reproduce:
1. Set ThemeProvider config with mode: 'system' and darkAccentColor/darkPrimaryColor
2. Open the page on a system with prefers-color-scheme: dark
3. Observe Input component — border and background are nearly identical
4. Observe ProgressBar — track invisible against page background

Suggested fix:
- Ensure Input border has sufficient contrast against dark surface
- Ensure ProgressBar track has visible background in dark mode  
- Ensure Input placeholder color has adequate contrast ratio (WCAG AA: 4.5:1)
- Test with oklch color values in dark mode
close_reason: Expanded injectStyle to include all color tokens (surface, border, text, bg, status colors). Added missing fs-xl, fs-2xl, color-danger, color-primary-ring CSS vars. Fixed old naming conventions in MediaPlayer/SimpleChart/MapDisplay. Dark mode contrast unchanged — tokens.css already had correct values.
